Then apply the quadratic formula: x = [-b ± √(b² - 4ac)] / (2a). Calculate the discriminant (b² - 4ac) to determine the nature of the roots—real or complex—and proceed accordingly.

Stationary points occur where the derivative of f(x), denoted as f'(x), equals zero. First, compute the derivative of f(x). Then set f'(x) = 0 and solve for x. These x-values are potential stationary points. To confirm their nature (maximum or minimum), check the second derivative at those points.
